name: Village
howToFind: Generates in plains, desert, savanna, taiga, snowy plains and meadow biomes (Bedrock adds snowy taiga and sunflower plains) - walk and look, or use /locate structure minecraft:village_plains (each variant has its own ID)
Cartographers sell explorer maps that point to villages
Villages are slightly more common in Bedrock than in Java
loot: Hay bales and farm crops
Loot chests whose contents depend on the building
Beds and workstations you can take for your own trading hall
dangers: Illager raids, triggered by entering a village with Bad Omen
Zombie sieges (Java): 10% chance at midnight or during thunderstorms in villages with at least 20 beds
Abandoned villages (2%) hold only zombie villagers, no doors or torches, and cobwebs
tips: Villagers ring the bell when a raid starts, and a bell marks a gathering site.
Villagers that link to a bed create the village; a village needs at least one linked bed to exist.
Source: minecraft.wiki Village.
keywords: village minecraft find loot bell raid zombie village

name: Stronghold
howToFind: Throw eyes of ender: they fly toward the nearest stronghold. Follow them until they start diving into the ground, then dig down
Triangulate: throw from two spots a few hundred blocks apart and walk to where the flight lines cross - saves eyes
Java: 128 strongholds generate in eight rings around the world origin (the first ring has 3, 1,280-2,816 blocks out). Bedrock: no limit, at least 160 blocks from the origin
loot: Chests in corridors and libraries: ender pearls (about 23% per chest), iron chestplates, rarely an enchanted book
The End portal room, the only room guaranteed in every stronghold
dangers: Silverfish spawner in the portal room - break it or light it before activating the portal
Silverfish hide in infested stone bricks throughout the structure
Easy to get lost: place torches on one side to mark the way back
tips: Bring enough eyes of ender for the frames and the trip.
Rarely the portal room is overwritten by a cave, monument or another structure: then find another stronghold.
Mine straight down only after digging a staircase - strongholds love to open into caves and ravines. Source: minecraft.wiki Stronghold.
keywords: stronghold find eyes of ender end portal silverfish library loot

name: Ancient City
howToFind: Generates in the deep dark biome, with its floor at Y=-51, often under mountains and other low-erosion areas
Dig down from a mountain or find a deep cave that reaches deepslate levels
/locate structure minecraft:ancient_city with cheats on
loot: Chests with items found nowhere else, such as disc fragments, armor trims and echo shards (craft the recovery compass)
A chest with a golden apple in the city center
dangers: Sculk sensors hear you walk, place and break blocks - sculk shriekers summon the Warden
The Warden: 500 HP, sonic boom attack that goes through walls and armor. You are not meant to fight it
tips: Bring stacks of wool: it dampens vibrations so sensors do not hear you.
If the Warden spawns: leave the way you came, quietly. Source: minecraft.wiki Ancient City.
keywords: ancient city deep dark warden loot echo shard swift sneak reinforced deepslate

name: Bastion Remnant
howToFind: Generates in nether wastes, soul sand valleys, crimson forests and warped forests (not basalt deltas: a fortress generates there instead)
Four types: bridges, hoglin stables, housing units and treasure rooms
/locate structure minecraft:bastion_remnant
loot: Loot chests in ramparts, stables and housing units; treasure rooms hold treasure chests on a lava basin
Blocks of gold and gilded blackstone
Piglins, piglin brutes and hoglins that spawn with the structure never despawn
dangers: Piglin brutes spawn only here when the structure generates, and do not despawn unless killed
Piglins and hoglins do not hunt each other
A magma cube spawner sits in the treasure room
tips: Clear the piglin brutes first: they do not despawn.
Hoglin stables hold hoglins that never despawn.
Never dig straight down in a bastion: lava is everywhere. Source: minecraft.wiki Bastion Remnant.
keywords: bastion remnant nether loot piglin brute netherite upgrade template pigstep treasure room

name: Nether Fortress
howToFind: Generates in all Nether biomes; the Nether is split into regions where either a fortress or a bastion remnant generates
Look for dark nether brick bridges over lava seas
/locate structure minecraft:fortress
loot: Nether wart growing beside stairways
Blaze spawners: blaze rods
Corridor chests (1/3 chance at each corridor turn): saddles, golden and iron horse armor, gold ingots, diamonds, flint and steel, golden swords
dangers: Fortresses are the only place wither skeletons and blazes spawn
Blazes set you on fire from range
One wrong step off a bridge into lava ends many runs
tips: Fortresses use their own mob list; surrounding soul sand valley or warped forest raises spawn rates (Java).
Light up the fortress to find the spawn spots; glass panes or iron bars keep mobs still. Source: minecraft.wiki Nether Fortress.
keywords: nether fortress find blaze spawner wither skeleton skull nether wart loot

name: Trial Chambers
howToFind: Underground structures of copper and tuff; the starting room generates between Y=-40 and -20, and most rooms between Y=-20 and 0
Buy a trial explorer map from a journeyman cartographer (12 emeralds + compass)
/locate structure minecraft:trial_chambers
loot: The only place where trial spawners and vaults generate naturally
Entrances have vaults and chests; the atrium always has an ominous vault above the entrance doorway
dangers: Trial spawners can summon zombies, husks, skeletons, strays, bogged, spiders, cave spiders, slimes, silverfish and breezes
Bad Omen turns into Trial Omen and makes all trial spawners ominous: harder, with greater rewards
tips: Some corridor spawners never spawn breezes.
Source: minecraft.wiki Trial Chambers.
keywords: trial chambers 1.21 breeze vault trial key heavy core mace ominous

name: Woodland Mansion
howToFind: Generates rarely in dark forests and pale gardens, often far from world spawn
Woodland explorer maps come from cartographer villagers and abandoned camp secret chests (26.3); a map may not point to the nearest mansion
/locate structure minecraft:mansion
loot: Evokers, one of the only sources of totems of undying
Imprisoned allays inside the mansion
Chests with random loot, plus wool, bookshelves and decorations
dangers: Vindicators: axe-wielding illagers, on every floor
Evokers (second floor and up): fangs and vexes
Most rooms are dark, so ordinary Overworld mobs can spawn inside or walk in at night
tips: Vindicators and evokers do not respawn once killed.
Light every room as you clear it.
Mansions have three floors; the first floor only holds vindicator rooms. Source: minecraft.wiki Woodland Mansion.
keywords: woodland mansion dark forest evoker vindicator totem allay explorer map

name: Ocean Monument
howToFind: Generates in deep ocean biomes (deep, deep frozen, deep cold, deep lukewarm; deep warm in Bedrock)
Buy an ocean explorer map from an apprentice-level cartographer, for emeralds
/locate structure minecraft:monument
loot: Block of gold in the treasure chamber
Wet sponges, from sponge rooms (about 30 on the ceiling; not every monument has one) - monuments are the only place sponges are found
Prismarine, dark prismarine and sea lanterns from the structure itself
dangers: Guardians spawn only in the monument area
Always three elder guardians: one at the top and one in each wing; they inflict Mining Fatigue III
tips: Kill the elders first, then mine.
The monument has at least six chambers and 23 pillars down to the seafloor. In Bedrock the roof is always at Y=56. Source: minecraft.wiki Ocean Monument.
keywords: ocean monument guardian elder sponge gold prismarine tide trim mining fatigue

name: Abandoned Mineshaft
howToFind: Generates underground in any Overworld biome except the deep dark, often intersecting caves
A dark oak variant generates on the surface in badlands biomes
/locate structure minecraft:mineshaft; mineshaft explorer maps come from secret chests in abandoned camps (added in 26.3)
loot: Chests always appear as a minecart with chest on rails: rails (78%), name tags, glow berries, seeds, powered/detector/activator rails, enchanted books (14%), diamonds (about 9%)
Cobwebs to shear for string
Cave spider spawners in abandoned passageways
dangers: Cave spider spawners hide behind cobwebs
Open drops and unsupported sections
tips: Badlands mineshafts are mostly above ground, with more complete rails; badlands also have plenty of gold ore.
Use torches to mark your way back. Source: minecraft.wiki Mineshaft.
keywords: abandoned mineshaft cave spider rails chest minecart cobweb badlands

name: Desert Temple (Pyramid)
howToFind: Generates in desert biomes (desert hills too in Bedrock); orange terracotta towers show above the dunes
/locate structure minecraft:desert_pyramid
Less frequent in Java than in Bedrock
loot: 4 chests hidden in a fosse under the center, rigged with a TNT trap: sand, enchanted books (22% per chest), emeralds, diamonds, diamond horse armor, enchanted golden apples (2.4% per chest)
A buried 5x5 side room with 6-8 suspicious sand blocks (brush them)
The temple itself: terracotta and cut sandstone
dangers: A stone pressure plate under the blue terracotta block triggers a 3x3 grid of TNT (9 blocks), which can kill you and destroy the chests
tips: Never step on the pressure plate: dig down beside it, or break the plate first.
The temple does have suspicious sand, in its buried side room.
Source: minecraft.wiki Desert Pyramid.
keywords: desert temple pyramid tnt trap chests golden apple horse armor

name: Jungle Temple
howToFind: Generates in jungles (not sparse jungles) and, in Java, bamboo jungles
/locate structure minecraft:jungle_pyramid
Jungle explorer maps are sold by desert, savanna and swamp cartographers
loot: Two chests: one at the end of the arrow-trap hallway, one revealed by the lever puzzle
Chest items: bones, gold and iron ingots, bamboo, diamonds (13%), emeralds, enchanted books (4%), horse armor
Dispensers, tripwire hooks, sticky pistons and redstone
dangers: Two tripwire lines trigger dispensers hidden behind vines (2-14 arrows each)
tips: The puzzle: 3 levers on chiseled stone bricks on the bottom floor; the right combination pulls away a block to reveal a chest.
Source: minecraft.wiki Jungle Pyramid.
keywords: jungle temple puzzle levers tripwire dispensers cocoa mossy cobblestone

name: Trail Ruins
howToFind: Buried structures in taiga, snowy taiga, old growth spruce and pine taiga, old growth birch forest and jungle; only the top of the tower shows above ground
/locate structure minecraft:trail_ruins
loot: Suspicious gravel blocks to brush
The only structures where mud bricks, packed mud and blocks of coal generate naturally
dangers: Some suspicious gravel generates floating: it falls and is destroyed if an adjacent block updates
tips: Brush the suspicious gravel instead of mining it.
The ruins have a main road of cobblestone, stone and stone bricks linking small buildings. Source: minecraft.wiki Trail Ruins.
keywords: trail ruins archaeology brush suspicious gravel pottery sherds armor trims host raiser shaper wayfinder

name: Abandoned Camp
howToFind: Added in Java 26.3 (Wilderness Bound, released September 15, 2026); Bedrock 26.50. Source: minecraft.net
Generates in eighteen Overworld surface biomes (forests, taiga, savanna, jungle, swamp, meadow, pale garden and more)
One generation attempt per 34x34-chunk region; camps are 8 to 60 chunks apart, 34.5 on average
/locate structure minecraft:abandoned_camp
loot: Chests and barrels: bones, coal, straw beds (about 35% per barrel in Java 26.3) and empty maps
Camp maps lead to other camps
Rare oxidized copper chests with better loot
dangers: Camp contents and loot tables differ slightly between Java and Bedrock
tips: The tent is made of white wool stairs; the campfire is unlit.
There are 10 tent variants per biome, for 8,820 possible camp configurations. Source: minecraft.wiki Abandoned Camp.
keywords: abandoned camp structure 26.3 wilderness bound explorer map tent straw bed cushion copper chest

name: End City
howToFind: On the large outer End islands where chorus trees grow, reached through the End gateway
/locate structure minecraft:end_city
loot: End ships: the only source of elytra (item frame in the treasure room) and dragon heads
Loot rooms with two chests (some have a normal chest next to an ender chest)
Resident shulkers
dangers: Shulkers: many spawn in skyscraper towers; three guard each ship
Parkour-like staircases and drops into the void
tips: Each tower direction has a 50% chance of a bridge, and each bridge a 12.5% chance of an End ship; at most one ship per city.
Source: minecraft.wiki End City.
keywords: end city elytra end ship shulker shell dragon head end gateway outer islands find

name: Pillager Outpost
howToFind: Generates in village biomes and also cherry grove, grove, snowy slopes and peaks
Semi-rare: every several hundred to a couple thousand blocks, rarer than villages, less rare than mansions. In Java never within villages
/locate structure minecraft:pillager_outpost
loot: Raid captains drop an ominous bottle of level 1-5; drinking it gives Bad Omen for 100 minutes
The watchtower chest sits on the top level
Cages hold an iron golem (85% chance) or allays (50% chance); they are optional side structures
dangers: Pillagers keep spawning around the outpost (Java: light level 8 or less, in a 72x58x72 area), even if you stand in the tower
A total of eight pillagers, including the captain, spawn at generation
tips: Drinking the bottle near a village starts a raid.
Up to four smaller structures spawn around the tower. Source: minecraft.wiki Pillager Outpost.
keywords: pillager outpost raid captain ominous bottle bad omen allay crossbow find

name: Ruined Portal
howToFind: Generates commonly in all Overworld biomes except the deep dark and in all Nether biomes: one per 640-block square (25-chunk area plus buffer)
Surrounded by netherrack; underground, on the surface or on the ocean floor depending on biome
/locate structure minecraft:ruined_portal
loot: A chest with gold items and portal-building items such as obsidian and flint and steel (in Java it may be replaced by terrain, often lava)
Blocks of gold next to the frame in most variants
dangers: Portals can sit over lava
Frames may contain crying obsidian, which cannot activate a Nether portal
tips: 13 variants: 10 normal and 3 giant portals.
You may need to supply missing obsidian yourself. Source: minecraft.wiki Ruined Portal.
keywords: ruined portal crying obsidian gold flint and steel chest loot nether overworld find

name: Shipwreck
howToFind: Generates commonly in all oceans; rarely on beaches, snowy beaches, or inside icebergs, ocean ruins, monuments or canyons
Upright, sideways or upside-down, often missing parts
/locate structure minecraft:shipwreck
loot: Up to 3 chests with different loot tables: supply chest in the bow, treasure chest in the upper stern, map chest in the lower stern
Supply chests: suspicious stew (54%), paper, wheat, carrots, potatoes, moss blocks, coal, enchanted leather armor (about 21% per piece), TNT (7.5%)
Map chests hold the buried treasure map
dangers: Drowning while looting; wrecks are often broken, so a chest may be missing
tips: The three chests depend on which sections are intact.
Source: minecraft.wiki Shipwreck.
keywords: shipwreck treasure map chest stern bow drowned ocean find suspicious stew

name: Buried Treasure
howToFind: Generates in beach and snowy beach biomes (Bedrock: also stony shore and mushroom field shore), sometimes on the ocean floor
Java: the chest is at chunk-section relative 9,9, facing east; Bedrock: 8,8
Buried treasure maps come from shipwreck map chests
loot: Always 1 heart of the sea (only source)
Iron ingots (99%), gold ingots (88%), cooked cod/salmon (75%), potion of Water Breathing (67%), TNT (63%)
Emeralds 4-8, prismarine crystals 1-5, diamonds 1-2 (each in about 53-60% of chests)
dangers: If exposed to water the chest is waterlogged; drowning while digging underwater
tips: Use F3 chunk coordinates to dig at 9,9 in Java.
The chest is almost always buried under sand or gravel (stone on underwater hills). Source: minecraft.wiki Buried Treasure.
keywords: buried treasure heart of the sea conduit map x marks chunk 9 9 dig beach

name: Swamp Hut
howToFind: Generates rarely in swamps (not mangrove swamps), in the north-west corner of a chunk
Swamp explorer maps are sold by jungle, snowy and taiga cartographers
/locate structure minecraft:swamp_hut
loot: Cauldron (empty in Java; 1-3 bottles of a random potion in Bedrock), crafting table, flower pot
One witch and one black cat spawn at generation and never despawn naturally (no witch on Peaceful)
dangers: Witches can spawn anywhere in the 7x7x9 area of the hut
tips: Witches and cats wander off; they do not return to the hut on purpose.
In Bedrock a killed witch respawns on one block, two blocks in front of the crafting table. Source: minecraft.wiki Swamp Hut.
keywords: swamp hut witch hut black cat cauldron witch farm slime full moon find

name: Ocean Ruins
howToFind: Cold ruins (stone bricks) in ocean, cold ocean and frozen ocean biomes and their deep variants; warm ruins (sandstone) in warm, lukewarm and deep lukewarm oceans
Mostly underwater, sometimes bordering a beach; 30% are large, and a large ruin has a 90% chance of 4-8 small ruins clustered around it
Explorer maps for warm ocean ruins come from abandoned camp chests (26.3); /locate structure minecraft:ocean_ruin_cold or minecraft:ocean_ruin_warm
loot: Chests in nearly every ruin: coal, wheat, gold nuggets and buried treasure maps (43% in big chests)
Suspicious gravel (cold) and suspicious sand (warm) to brush: pottery sherds, nautilus armor, emeralds (warm ruins also sniffer eggs)
dangers: Persistent drowned (usually 1-2 per structure), some riding zombie nautiluses with tridents
Ruins can be partly buried, with suspicious blocks under normal gravel, sand or stone
tips: Zombie nautiluses spawned by ruins even appear on Peaceful.
Brush the suspicious blocks instead of mining them. Source: minecraft.wiki Cold Ocean Ruins and Warm Ocean Ruins.
keywords: ocean ruins underwater structure drowned suspicious gravel treasure map pottery sherds nautilus armor find

name: Igloo
howToFind: Generates uncommonly in snowy plains, snowy taiga and snowy slopes
Half of all igloos have an oak trapdoor under the third carpet from the doorway (the others have a snow block there)
/locate structure minecraft:igloo
loot: Inside: bed, furnace, crafting table, redstone torch
Basement (50% of igloos): a villager and a zombie villager in cells, a brewing stand, a cauldron and a chest with a golden apple (100%)
dangers: Some basement stone bricks are infested blocks with silverfish
tips: In Java the villager is unemployed (plains type); in Bedrock it is snowy with a random profession.
In Bedrock an igloo with a basement counts as a village, so a raid can trigger there. Source: minecraft.wiki Igloo.
keywords: igloo basement trapdoor zombie villager cure golden apple weakness potion snowy find silverfish

name: Monster Room
howToFind: Generates uncommonly underground in any Overworld biome, always near caves, canyons, mineshafts or strongholds
A cobblestone room with mossy cobblestone floor (75% of floor cobblestone), 7 or 9 blocks wide
Spawner in the center
loot: Up to 2 chests: bones, gunpowder, rotten flesh, string (58% each), wheat, bread, coal, redstone, leather, name tags (25%), music discs 13 and cat, golden apples (19%), iron ingots, buckets, enchanted books (13%)
Spawner: zombie 50%, skeleton 25%, spider 25% (Bedrock zombie spawners can also produce zombie villagers, 5%)
dangers: Mobs keep spawning in the room until it is lit or the spawner is removed
tips: Mobs spawn up to 4 blocks from the spawner, even outside the room walls if there is open space. Source: minecraft.wiki Monster Room.
keywords: monster room dungeon spawner zombie skeleton spider chest loot music disc name tag XP farm find

name: Amethyst Geode
howToFind: Generates underground in any Overworld biome between Y=-58 and Y=30; each chunk has a 1/24 chance to attempt one
Look for the smooth basalt outer layer with calcite under it
/locate structure minecraft:amethyst_geode
loot: Amethyst cluster: 4 shards with a pickaxe; any tool with Silk Touch drops the cluster or bud itself
Amethyst buds drop nothing without Silk Touch; only fully grown clusters drop shards
Amethyst blocks, smooth basalt and calcite
dangers: Budding amethyst makes up 8.3% of the inner layer and grows buds
tips: A bud placed on budding amethyst grows through small, medium and large stages into a cluster; an unobstructed face takes about 2 hours to fully regrow on average.
Do not break buds early. Source: minecraft.wiki Amethyst Geode and Amethyst Cluster.
keywords: amethyst geode minecraft find shards budding amethyst cluster calcite smooth basalt spyglass tinted glass fortune

name: Fossil
howToFind: Generates rarely underground in desert, swamp and mangrove swamp biomes - skull or spine shapes made of bone blocks
Two generation attempts per chunk at 1/64 each: one range Y 0 to 320 (with coal ore), one Y -63 to -8 (with diamond ore below Y -8)
No map and no /locate support for the small features - strip mine in a swamp or desert and watch for bone blocks
loot: Bone blocks
Coal ore embedded in fossils above Y=0
Diamond ore (Java) and deepslate diamond ore below Y=-8
dangers: Structure integrity 0.9: about 10% of the bone blocks are missing
Deep fossils sit in deepslate layers with lava pockets
tips: Each chunk has two attempts at 1/64 (Y 0 to 320, and Y -63 to -8). Source: minecraft.wiki Fossil.
keywords: fossil minecraft desert swamp bone block diamond ore coal find bone meal skull spine

name: Desert Well
howToFind: Generates in desert biomes (desert hills and lakes too in Bedrock), on sand over solid ground
It is a structure-like feature, not a full structure
Look for a small sandstone well with water inside
loot: Two suspicious sand blocks under the water, each with one item: pottery sherds (arms up and brewer, 25% each), brick, emerald, stick or suspicious stew (12.5% each)
dangers: None
tips: Bring a brush: every well has suspicious sand.
Suspicious sand under desert wells was added in 1.20. Source: minecraft.wiki Desert Well.
keywords: desert well minecraft suspicious sand brush pottery sherds archaeology water feature
